content: Nephritis refers to the inflammation of the kidney. The term is derived from the Greek words nephromeaning of the kidney and -itis meaning inflammation. There are several subtypes of nephritis, each affecting different parts of the kidney: 1. Glomerulonephritis: This is the inflammation of the glomeruli, which are the tiny filtering units within the kidney. When the term nephritis is used without further specification, it often refers to this particular condition. 2. Interstitial nephritis (or tubulo-interstitial nephritis): This subtype involves inflammation of the spaces between the renal tubules, which are structures responsible for filtering and reabsorbing substances in the kidney. 3. Pyelonephritis: This occurs when a urinary tract infection progresses to involve the renal pelvis (pyelum) of the kidney, leading to inflammation. 4. Lupus nephritis: This is a form of kidney inflammation caused by systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), an autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks the body's own tissues, including the kidneys. Certain medications are known to cause nephritis as a side effect. These include: Nivolumab: An immune checkpoint inhibitor used in cancer therapy. Sulfasalazine: A drug commonly used to treat inflammatory bowel disease and rheumatoid arthritis. Oxacillin: A beta-lactam antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections. Nephritis is also associated with other medical conditions, such as Bright's disease and Wegener's granulomatosis (now more commonly referred to as granulomatosis with polyangiitis).
